instructions:
### Heading hierarchy:
ALL section headings must use exactly six hash marks (######).
Within any section body, sub-elements that need visual labels (problem titles in Assessment & Plan, subsection labels in Objective, etc.) must use **bold text** (`**Label**`), not heading-level markdown.
Every heading must be followed by a blank line (double newline) before body content.
### Missing information:
If an entire section has no supported content, use `Not Provided`. Omit unsupported subsections and optional details.
---
### Current vs Prior Information:
The focus of every note is the current encounter. When prior encounter information is referenced, explicitly indicate it using language such as "Previously…", "At last visit…", "Per prior records…". Do not blend prior and current encounter data without this explicit tagging.

Use supplied facts only. Do not infer absent facts or copy clinical facts from illustrative examples.
---
### Note type:
This is an outpatient dermatology note for medical, procedural, and skin cancer screening visits.
### Lesion fidelity:
Record lesion location, laterality, size, morphology, color, and dermoscopic features exactly as stated. Do not convert sizes, add descriptors, or suggest a diagnosis the clinician did not name. When several lesions are discussed, keep the same lesion number and site label in Skin Examination, Procedures, and Assessment and Plan.

sections.title: Chief Complaint
sections.instructions:
**Purpose and sources**
Capture the reason(s) for the visit as stated by the patient or clinician.
**Organization and format**
- Use `- item` bullets with a short label including body site when stated (for example, `- Changing mole, left upper back`).
**Examples**
Illustrative only; do not copy clinical facts.
Input: Patient: "I'm here for my yearly skin check, and there's a spot on my nose that keeps bleeding."
Output:
```text
- Annual skin cancer screening
- Bleeding spot on the nose
```

sections.title: History of Present Illness
sections.instructions:
**Purpose and sources**
Document the patient-reported history of each skin concern.
**Include**
- Onset and duration, evolution (growth, color or shape change), symptoms (itch, pain, bleeding, burning), triggers, and distribution or spread.
- Prior treatments with product, strength, duration, and response, as reported.
- For rashes: exposures, new products, contacts with similar rash, systemic symptoms.
- For acne or chronic conditions: course since last visit, adherence, side effects.
**Exclude and placement**
- Exam findings and dermoscopy belong in Skin Examination. Decisions belong in Assessment and Plan.
**Organization and format**
Group by concern using a bold label and concise bullets, separated by blank lines.
**Examples**
Illustrative only; do not copy clinical facts.
Input: Patient: "The spot on my nose showed up about 6 months ago. It scabs over, bleeds when I wash my face, then comes back. It doesn't hurt. I tried Neosporin for a couple weeks, no change."
Output:
```text
**Bleeding lesion, nose**

- Present for about six months.
- Recurrently scabs and bleeds with face washing; not painful.
- Topical antibiotic ointment for about two weeks without improvement.
```

sections.title: Dermatologic and Medical History
sections.instructions:
**Purpose and sources**
Document dermatologic, medical, family, and social history pertinent to skin care.
**Include**
- **Dermatologic History:** Prior skin cancers (type, site, year, treatment), atypical nevi, prior biopsies, chronic skin conditions, phototherapy.
- **Medical History:** Immunosuppression, organ transplant, bleeding disorders, pacemaker or defibrillator (relevant to electrosurgery), and other relevant conditions.
- **Family History:** Melanoma and other skin cancers or skin conditions in relatives.
- **Sun Exposure and Social History:** Sunburn history, tanning bed use, outdoor occupation or hobbies, sunscreen use, tobacco.
- **Pregnancy and Contraception:** When relevant to treatment (for example, isotretinoin or retinoids).
**Organization and format**
Use the bold labels above with `- item` bullets. Omit labels without supported information.
**Examples**
Illustrative only; do not copy clinical facts.
Input: Patient: "I had a basal cell on my back cut out in 2020. My dad had melanoma. I'm a landscaper and I never really wear sunscreen. I have a pacemaker."
Output:
```text
**Dermatologic History**

- Basal cell carcinoma of the back, excised: 2020.

**Medical History**

- Pacemaker.

**Family History**

- Father: Melanoma.

**Sun Exposure and Social History**

- Works as a landscaper; rarely uses sunscreen.
```

sections.title: Medications
sections.instructions:
**Purpose and sources**
Document current medications before today's changes, including topicals, systemic dermatologic drugs, and medications that affect procedures (anticoagulants, antiplatelets, immunosuppressants).
**Include**
- Name, strength, vehicle for topicals, site, and frequency when stated.
**Exclude and placement**
- Medications started or changed today belong in Assessment and Plan.
**Organization and format**
- Use `- item` bullets: `[Name] [strength] [vehicle or route] [site if stated] [frequency]`.
**Examples**
Illustrative only; do not copy clinical facts.
Input: Patient: "I use triamcinolone cream 0.1% on my elbows twice a day when they flare, and I take Eliquis."
Output:
```text
- Triamcinolone 0.1% cream to elbows twice daily as needed for flares.
- Apixaban.
```

sections.title: Allergies
sections.instructions:
**Purpose and sources**
Document the patient's allergies as provided in the transcript.
**Include**
- Capture the allergen name AND the reaction if available.
- Include all allergies mentioned (medications, environmental, food, etc.).
**Organization and format**
- Use `- item` bullet format if multiple allergies.
- Format each entry as: `[Allergen]: [Reaction if stated]`.
**Missing information**
If allergy information was not discussed in the transcript, use `Not Provided`.
**Examples**
Illustrative only; do not copy clinical facts.
Input: Patient: “Penicillin gives me hives. I'm also allergic to shellfish, but I don't remember the reaction.”
Output:
```text
- Penicillin: Hives.
- Shellfish
```
- Include adhesive, latex, lidocaine or other local anesthetic, and antiseptic (for example, chlorhexidine) reactions when stated, since they affect procedures.

sections.title: Skin Examination
sections.instructions:
**Purpose and sources**
Document the clinician's skin examination and dermoscopic findings.
**Include**
- **Exam Scope:** Full-body skin exam or focused exam, areas examined, and areas the patient declined, when stated. Fitzpatrick skin type when stated.
- **Lesions:** For each discussed lesion: anatomic location with laterality, size (in mm or cm as stated), primary morphology (macule, papule, plaque, nodule, vesicle, pustule, patch), color, shape and borders, surface change (scale, crust, ulceration), and distribution for rashes.
- **Dermoscopy:** Structures and patterns as stated (for example, arborizing vessels, atypical pigment network, regression structures, blue-white veil).
- **Other Findings:** Hair, nails, mucosa, lymph nodes, and incidental benign lesions the clinician names (for example, seborrheic keratoses, cherry angiomas).
**Exclude and placement**
- Patient-reported symptoms belong in History of Present Illness. Diagnoses and clinical impressions belong in Assessment and Plan, except a brief descriptive label stated during the exam.
**Organization and format**
Begin with `**Exam Scope**` as a single bullet. Then one bold block per lesion, `**Lesion [n]: [Site]**`, with bullets for Size, Morphology, Color, Borders or Surface, and Dermoscopy as supported. End with `**Other Findings**` when present.
**Examples**
Illustrative only; do not copy clinical facts.
Input: Clinician: "Full skin exam today. On the right nasal ala there's a 6 millimeter pearly pink papule with central crust. On dermoscopy, arborizing vessels and a small ulceration. Scattered seborrheic keratoses on the trunk."
Output:
```text
**Exam Scope**

- Full-body skin examination.

**Lesion 1: Right nasal ala**

- Size: 6 mm.
- Morphology: Papule with central crust.
- Color: Pearly pink.
- Dermoscopy: Arborizing vessels and small ulceration.

**Other Findings**

- Scattered seborrheic keratoses on the trunk.
```

sections.title: Procedures
sections.instructions:
**Purpose and sources**
Document each procedure performed today, as stated by the clinician.
**Include**
- Procedure type (for example, shave biopsy, tangential biopsy, punch biopsy with size, excision with margins, cryotherapy with number of lesions and freeze-thaw cycles, electrodesiccation and curettage, intralesional injection with drug and concentration).
- Site with laterality and lesion number, matching Skin Examination.
- Indication or clinical differential when stated.
- Consent: Risks, benefits, and alternatives discussed and consent obtained (verbal or written), only when stated.
- Preparation, anesthesia (agent, concentration, volume), hemostasis method, closure (suture type and number), and dressing.
- Specimen: Labeling, container, and destination (for example, sent to dermatopathology).
- Estimated blood loss, complications, and patient tolerance when stated.
- Wound care instructions given.
**Exclude and placement**
- Procedures planned for a future visit belong in Assessment and Plan.
**Organization and format**
One bold block per procedure, `**[Procedure], [Site]**`, with `- **Label:** Content` bullets in this order: Indication, Consent, Anesthesia, Technique, Hemostasis, Closure, Specimen, Complications, Wound Care. Omit labels without supported information.
**Missing information**
Never state that consent was obtained, a time-out was performed, or there were no complications unless the transcript says so. If no procedure was performed, use `Not Provided`.
**Examples**
Illustrative only; do not copy clinical facts.
Input: Clinician: "We talked about the risks of bleeding, infection, and scarring, and you agreed. I numbed it with 1 mL of 1% lidocaine with epinephrine, did a shave biopsy of the right nasal ala lesion, aluminum chloride for bleeding. Specimen is going to dermpath labeled A, right nasal ala. Keep Vaseline and a bandage on it daily until healed."
Output:
```text
**Shave biopsy, right nasal ala (Lesion 1)**

- **Consent:** Risks of bleeding, infection, and scarring discussed; patient agreed.
- **Anesthesia:** 1 mL of 1% lidocaine with epinephrine.
- **Hemostasis:** Aluminum chloride.
- **Specimen:** Labeled A, right nasal ala; sent to dermatopathology.
- **Wound Care:** Petrolatum and a bandage daily until healed.
```

sections.title: Assessment and Plan
sections.instructions:
**Purpose and sources**
Document the dermatologist's assessments and plans. Write directly from the clinician's perspective.
**Include**
- Each diagnosis or clinical impression, with the lesion number and site when relevant, and stated differential (for example, "favor basal cell carcinoma; rule out squamous cell carcinoma").
- How pathology results will be communicated and the next step for each result when stated.
- Skin-care plan: photoprotection, moisturizers, gentle cleansers, and avoidance of triggers, as discussed.
- Medication counseling, including application amount, duration limits for topical steroids, and monitoring for systemic agents (for example, iPLEDGE requirements and labs for isotretinoin).
**Organization and format**
Each block: **bold diagnosis** (with site), optional one-sentence assessment, then `- **Label**: Content` bullets in this order:
- **Plan**: Selected actions, pathology follow-up, contingencies.
- **Procedures**: Reference procedures performed today (for example, "Shave biopsy performed today; see Procedures") or planned procedures.
- **Tests**: Labs or other studies ordered.
- **Medications**: Action, name, strength, vehicle, site, frequency, and duration.
- **Skin Care**: Specific products or measures (for example, broad-spectrum SPF 30+ daily, fragrance-free emollient twice daily).
- **Referrals**: Mohs surgery or other services, with reason.
- **Follow Up**: Timeframe, including next full-skin exam interval when stated.
**Examples**
Illustrative only; do not copy clinical facts.
Input: Clinician: "The nose lesion looks like a basal cell; we biopsied it and I'll call you with results in about a week. If it's confirmed, I'll send you for Mohs. Use SPF 30 or higher every morning and reapply outside. For the psoriasis on your elbows, keep the triamcinolone but no more than two weeks at a time. Full skin check in 6 months."
Output:
```text
**Lesion 1, right nasal ala, suspected basal cell carcinoma**

- **Plan**: Results by phone in about one week.
- **Procedures**: Shave biopsy performed today; see Procedures.
- **Referrals**: Mohs surgery if basal cell carcinoma is confirmed.

**Psoriasis, elbows**

- **Medications**: Continue triamcinolone 0.1% cream; limit use to two weeks at a time.

**Skin cancer screening**

- **Skin Care**: Broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher every morning; reapply when outdoors.
- **Follow Up**: Full-body skin examination in six months.
```
